ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There is a graticule in the figure, with latitude marked approximately from 45°N to 50°N and longitude approximately near 122°E to 125°E; the equal-days lines of seasonally frozen soil as a whole roughly extend east-west and bend in local areas. Then reason: The equal-days lines are generally arranged along the east-west direction, indicating that the number of days of seasonally frozen soil mainly changes with latitude in the north-south direction, essentially reflecting the latitudinal difference in heat conditions. The question stem has already given that another influencing factor is the topographic factor, so the blank should be filled with "latitude factor."
